clue.text: Only partially support football player

parts.note: something done only partially is done by half
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A grudging fan offers only half-hearted support to a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only partially support' reads as a verb phrase but is two pieces, HALF and BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-back is a player positioned between the forwards and the defenders in football and rugby.

clue.text: In this place with jerks and unorthodox types

parts.note: here means in this place
tics are involuntary twitches or jerks

explanation.surface: Odd, twitchy nonconformists have gathered here.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretics hold beliefs at odds with accepted doctrine, so they are unorthodox people.

clue.text: Plain refusal has everyone upset at first

indicators.note: says the reversed piece comes first, before the refusal
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word for everyone reads upwards

parts.note: all means everyone
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A blunt refusal upsets everyone at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where the reversed word reads upwards; 'at first' moves that piece ahead of the refusal even though the clue names it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassland in South America, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Club first to cover electronic material

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above covers the one below, so 1st sits on top of the E

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket
1st, written IST, is first
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A club is first to wrap something electronic in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Batiste is a fine, light cotton or linen fabric.

clue.text: Conservative to quarrel and brag

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, Britain's Tory party
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A Tory politician picks a fight and boasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, like a cockerel's call.

clue.text: Hollow container dumped by river

parts.note: a crate is a box for carrying goods
R is a standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Someone has dumped an empty box on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped depression in the ground, a kind of hollow.

clue.text: At hotel taking part outside in beastly space

indicators.note: the inner pieces take the word for part around them
the word for part sits outside the other letters

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: At a hotel, someone plays a part outside a horrible room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' suggests a nasty room, but the space literally belongs to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is a hole made by a rodent, and figuratively any squalid cramped place.

clue.text: Steamy row disturbed boy in book

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown into disorder, so Steamy row is rearranged

explanation.surface: A heated argument upset a young lad in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's novel centres on a mischievous boy growing up on the Mississippi.

clue.text: Expensive car that goes over part of cricket field

definitions.text: that goes over part of cricket field
definitions.meaning: a heavy cylinder drawn over the pitch to flatten it

explanation.surface: A luxury car drives across the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The pitch is the strip in the middle of a cricket ground where the ball is bowled, flattened by a heavy roller.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a Rolls-Royce and also the machine used to level a cricket pitch.

clue.text: Responses from one racist out of order

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled, so the words one racist are rearranged

explanation.surface: People respond angrily to one person's racist remark, which was out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as a judgement on the racist (British slang for unacceptable), but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are the ways people respond to something, so they are responses.

clue.text: Fish due to be tracked covertly

parts.note: a shad is a fish of the herring family
money owed is money due

explanation.surface: A fish is about to be followed in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shadowed is to be followed secretly, like a suspect tailed by a detective.

clue.text: Language that a militant uses

indicators.note: the phrase that a militant uses, read literally, contains the letters inside it

explanation.surface: We are asked which language a militant speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'that a militant': thaT A MILitant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: OT's aim to represent a religion

indicators.note: the letters of OT's aim are made to represent something else by being rearranged

explanation.surface: The Old Testament's purpose is to stand for a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the usual abbreviation for the Old Testament, but here its letters simply join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is a Chinese philosophical and spiritual tradition, one of the world's faiths.

clue.text: Explorer taking time to offer transport services

parts.note: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who sailed to North America for England in 1497
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A seafarer takes time out to offer people rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabotage is the carrying of goods or passengers between ports or points within one country, a trade in shipping.

clue.text: Old cook covered in fat was particularly noticeable

indicators.note: the old cook is covered in the word for fat, placed inside it

parts.note: stout means fat
to do food is to cook it, as in doing the potatoes

explanation.surface: An elderly chef smothered in grease was hard to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stood out was conspicuous, catching the eye more than its surroundings.

clue.text: Sweet things, yet of concern, I fancy

indicators.note: an elaborate, fanciful version of the letters of yet of concern, I is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: Someone admits a liking for sugary treats while worrying about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I like', but 'fancy' is the anagram signal and 'I' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery is the collective word for sweets and candies.

clue.text: Horrible quality of unusual stain on head

indicators.note: an unusual version of the word stain has its letters rearranged

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's shores

explanation.surface: A strange mark on someone's head has an ugly look.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is the state of being unpleasant or spiteful.

clue.text: Supported, as one is after the match

definitions.text: as one is after the match
definitions.meaning: married, the match being a marriage

explanation.surface: Backed up, as you are once the game has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sporting fixture, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse is both to adopt and champion a cause and, archaically, to marry.

clue.text: Lay heart(s) bare?

parts.note: to lay one's heart bare is to reveal one's intentions; at the card table, laying hearts face up reveals one's hand

explanation.definitionFit: Revealing your hand, literally at cards or figuratively in a negotiation, means disclosing your plans openly.

clue.text: Wild animals munched oranges

indicators.note: munched food is chewed up, so the letters of oranges are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Some untamed beasts chomped on citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses native to Asia.

clue.text: Companion leading Queen over lake or some other water

indicators.note: the companion leads, coming before the queen
in a down clue the queen is placed over, above, the lake

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A companion guides the Queen across a lake or another stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lake or some other water' looks like a single definition, but 'lake' gives L and only 'some other water' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a strait or watercourse, a body of water other than a lake.

clue.text: City observed after conflict

indicators.note: the word for observed comes after the conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A city seen in the aftermath of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland, largely rebuilt after the Second World War.

clue.text: Artist shows beast with no tail by hill

indicators.note: a word with no tail has lost its final letter, here the last letter of the synonym for beast

parts.note: a beast is an animal
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A painter exhibits a tailless creature next to a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like the artist exhibiting, but it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator is an artist who draws or models the frames of cartoons and films.

clue.text: Design military display

definitions.meaning: a picture or pattern inked into the skin
an outdoor show of marching bands and drill, as at Edinburgh

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an inked skin pattern and a ceremonial army performance, like the Edinburgh one.

clue.text: Hats left among other items of clothing

indicators.note: the letter for left goes among, inside, the clothing items

parts.note: ties are neckwear, other clothing items besides hats

explanation.surface: Hats are left with the rest of the clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is dated British slang for a hat, especially a top hat or bowler.

clue.text: Bouncy story with very little content

indicators.note: the abbreviation is the content of the word for story, held inside it

parts.note: a story is a lie, as in telling stories
V, a little abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A lively tale that has barely any substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A live ball is lively and springy, so it is bouncy.

clue.text: European plant with edible root

definitions.meaning: a large yellow-fleshed root vegetable, called rutabaga in North America

explanation.surface: A European plant whose root can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person from Sweden and the turnip-like vegetable known in America as rutabaga.

clue.text: Instruments to make geometric shapes

definitions.meaning: steel percussion instruments struck with a beater

explanation.surface: Tools for drawing figures in geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drawing instruments such as set squares; the instruments are the orchestral percussion kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bent-metal percussion instrument and a three-sided plane figure.

clue.text: Most well-thought-out point is being accepted

indicators.note: the word is is taken in, received inside the compass point

parts.note: west is one of the cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: The most carefully reasoned argument is the one that wins acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: The wisest course is the most sensible and judicious one, the best considered.

clue.text: Dealer is excited — what's converted into cash?

definitions.note: a past participle: assets that have been turned into money

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so Dealer is is rearranged

explanation.surface: An eager dealer wonders what has been sold for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are realised when they are sold and turned into money.
